title: Find Maximal Uncovered Ranges
summary: Given an integer n representing the length of an array nums, and a 2D-array ranges indicating sub-ranges of nums, find all maximal length uncovered ranges.
statement: Given an integer n representing the length of an array nums, and a 2D-array ranges indicating sub-ranges of nums, find all maximal length uncovered ranges. Each range in ranges is defined by two cells: start and end. The uncovered ranges must be sorted by their starting point in ascending order. An uncovered range is maximal if every cell belongs to exactly one sub-range and no two ranges (l1, r1) and (l2, r2) exist such that r1 + 1 equals l2.
constraints: Array indices run from zero through n-1; each inclusive input range is covered.
Return every maximal consecutive interval containing only uncovered indices.
Sort returned intervals by their starting index.
hints: Track the farthest covered endpoint seen so far.
A gap exists when the next start is more than one beyond that endpoint; add the trailing gap after the scan.
Taking the maximum endpoint merges overlaps and nesting, while each emitted gap is bounded by covered positions or array edges and is therefore maximal.
